abstract: Every year, 45,000 forest fires occur in Europe, destroying a forested surface area equivalent to the size of Belgium. Nearly 60\% of the forest fires have been ascribed to arson,, for this reason the so-called environmental crime has been included in the legal codes of the members of the European Union. For instance, in Spain forest fires are objects of prosecution in a court of law. This study analyzes the following variables: conservatism, dogmatism, locus of control, attitude toward the legal system, factors from the short Neuroticism Extraversion Openness Inventory (responsibility, openness, extraversion,, kindness), specific variables in the particular cases proposed (forest fires),, attitude toward the protection, improvement of the environment. The specific variables used in each case may help in better delineating verdict trends.

title: Information source, valence: How information credibility influences earthquake risk perception
authors: Zhu, Dongqing, Xie, Xiaofei, Gan, Yiqun
keywords: Wenchun earthquake; Information credibility; Information valence; Information source; Risk perception;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: The present research aims at the relationship between information credibility, perception of seismic risk in a group of people living in severe disaster areas. 243 adult residents exposed to seismic hazard participated in a questionnaire study. With respect to four types of information which are generated by information sources, valence, participants were instructed to recall one type of the information they obtained respectively, rate the recalled information in terms of its credibility. After that, they were asked to report their seismic risk perception, all socio-demographic data were also collected. Regression analyses suggested that information credibility significantly influenced risk perception. Furthermore, the credibility of word-of-mouth, negative information were positively associated with risk perception. Meanwhile, risk perception was also affected greatly by the credibility of negative public information but not positive word-of-mouth information. It was clear that both information source, valence moderated the process, the latter exerted a stronger influence on it. The results were interpreted in relation to the elaboration likelihood model, accessibility–diagnosticity model,, other cognitive theories. The findings were discussed in terms of their general implications for the improvement of risk communication about earthquake related messages.

title: Is there a place for social capital in the psychology of health, place?
authors: Wood, Lisa, Giles-Corti, Billie
keywords: ENVIRONMENTAL psychology; INFRASTRUCTURE (Economics); NEIGHBORHOOD; HARNESS;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: The field of environmental psychology is primely placed to further understanding of the way in which social capital influences or is influenced by the context, characteristics of neighbourhood environments, but has been one of the quieter voices in the cacophony of social capital discourse over the last decade. While there is increasing research interest in area, neighbourhood variations in social capital, the mechanisms, causal pathways through which physical environments, social capital, health may be related are not yet clear. More refined unpacking of the relationship between social capital, neighbourhood design, features, settings is required to identify practical intervention points for preserving, fostering, harnessing social capital within communities. Through a review of literature, this paper explores whether there is a place for social capital in the psychology of place, considers the contribution that environmental psychology, related disciplines could make to future social capital research, applications.

title: An ecological perspective on theory, methods,, analysis in environmental psychology: Advances, challenges
authors: Winkel, Gary, Saegert, Susan, Evans, Gary W
keywords: Analysis; Ecological Factors; Environmental Psychology; Ecological Psychology; Human; ecological perspectives; theory; methods;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Over the course of environmental psychology's brief history, there has been an interest in ecologically oriented approaches to theory, research. Based on this work, this paper identifies a set of six principles of ecological analysis that present theoretical, methodological,, analytic challenges to future research in environmental psychology. These challenges include the theoretical treatment of the multiple contexts within which human experience, behavior occurs, the need for sampling both persons, environments, the modeling of moderating, mediating processes, the issue of self-selection into, out of different settings, the necessity of considering temporal factors in environmental research, reliance on single methods (e.g., verbal report) in data generation, cross-sectional, longitudinal research designs,, the need for greater use of statistical techniques developed for contextual (multi-level) research. These issues are discussed, illustrated using recent developments in environmentally oriented research. The paper concludes with a set of 11 recommendations for the future.

title: Community noise problems: Evidence against adaptation
authors: Weinstein, Neil D
keywords: adaptation; Community Attitudes; Environmental Adaptation; Environmental Psychology; Noise Effects;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: It is commonly believed that people adapt rather easily to noise. This article reviews the available research, finding little evidence that any adaptation occurs in community settings. Much of this research, however, is open to alternative interpretations. The present study, examining reactions to traffic noise from the opening of a major new highway, was designed to remedy many of the problems with previous research. The investigation incorporated both a repeated measures design (the same respondents were interviewed 4, 16 months after the highway opening), an independent groups design (separate groups were interviewed either 4 or 16 months after opening). In addition, a pre-opening interview was carried out with the repeated measures panel. There was no evidence of appreciable adaptation in self-reported noise effects, annoyance, or tendency to focus attention on the noise. Instead respondents became more pessimistic about their ability to adapt to noise as time went by.

title: Perception of environmental risks of company sites
authors: Weber, Olaf
keywords: environmental risk; photographs; company sites; perception; Environmental Effects; Risk Perception;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: What are the stimulus properties that affect risk? Is it possible to assess the environmental risk of an industrial site by analysing the company's site or a photograph of the site? Often banks do this kind of inspection in case of a credit application or for new insurance contracts to judge environmentally caused credit risks. Both from the scientific, from the practical point of view it would be useful if a valid assessment of environmental risks of company sites done by visual perception could be done, including which environmental stimuli are affecting risk cognition in this field. To analyse this kind of perception of the manmade environment by visual stimuli, we tested the influence of the stimuli order, brightness, big structures, Gestalt, modernity, borders, newness in a quasi-experimental design with 54 participants, half of them bankers, half of them students. As control variables we used some personal, societal variables often linked to risk cognition. We presented 21 photographs of company sites to each participant for a fixed amount of time. Each participant had to judge the environmental risk of the sites. In addition, we assessed the perception of different stimuli, personality variables connected with risk perception. We found that bankers, students differ in their risk estimations, that stimulus characteristics were unstable, varying in their salience by site but not by persons. We identified objects, stimuli, which also increased or decreased environmental risk perception. Personality characteristics were inconsequential. The findings are usable for training measures for persons who have to judge environmental risks of sites. More research has to be done to identify stimuli affecting risk perception, cognition of manmade environments, to analyse the connection between stimuli, site characteristics.

title: Experimental evidence for a dual pathway model analysis of coping with the climate crisis
authors: van Zomeren, Martijn, Spears, Russell, Leach, Colin Wayne
keywords: Fear; Group efficacy; Environmental action; Coping; Collective action;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Two experiments examined the psychological power of fear, group efficacy beliefs to increase environmental action intentions against the climate crisis. Extending a dual pathway model of coping with collective disadvantage, results showed evidence for emotion-focused approach coping: Environmental action intentions were increased by individuals' manipulated fear of the negative future consequences of the climate crisis (Experiments 1–2). Additionally, results showed evidence for problem-focused approach coping: Individuals' measured (Experiment 1), manipulated group efficacy beliefs (Experiment 2) increased environmental action intentions. The results thus suggest that the dual pathway model can be successfully applied to a psychological analysis of emotion-, problem-focused approach coping with the climate crisis. We discuss the theoretical, practical implications of these results.

title: Place, identity processes
authors: Twigger-Ross, Clare L, Uzzell, David L
keywords: continuity \& self-efficacy \& distinctiveness \& self-esteem, attachment to residential environment, 26-67 yr olds, England; Attachment Behavior; Communities; Self Concept; Self Efficacy; Self Esteem; Environment;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: This paper examines the role of place, identity processes using Breakwell's model as a framework. This model suggests that there are four principles of identity which guide action: continuity, self-esteem, self-efficacy, distinctiveness. These principles are examined here in relation to attachment to a residential environment. It focuses on residents living in an area of the London Docklands, chosen because of the social, environmental, economic change in that area. It was hypothesized that attached respondents would discuss their relationship with the local environment in ways which supported or developed the identity principles whereas nonattached residents would not consider the local environment in this way. Twenty in-depth semi-structured interviews were carried out on a sample of residents from Rotherhithe in the London Docklands. The interviews were transcribed, content analysed. Results showed that there were differences between the attached, nonattached respondents in their discussion of their local environment. In addition, there were differences within the nonattached group such that some residents were not attached, neutral with regards to their residential environment, whereas others were not attached but had a negative evaluation of their residential environment. These results are discussed within the identity process model framework.

title: How organizational motives, communications affect public trust in organizations: The case of carbon dioxide capture, storage
authors: Terwel, Bart W, Harinck, Fieke, Ellemers, Naomi, Daamen, Dancker D L
keywords: Trust; Honesty; Motives; Communication; Climate change; CCS technology;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Preventing climate change is among the greatest environmental challenges facing the world today. Recently developed carbon dioxide capture, storage (CCS) technology is an important strategy to mitigate climate change. Public trust in organizations involved in CCS technology is important for successful implementation of this technology. This work adresses how inferred organizational motives, organizational communications affect public trust in these organizations. Study 1 (N = 264) showed that Dutch citizens generally have less trust in the industrial organizations than in the environmental NGOs involved in CCS. As predicted, inferred organizational motives (organization-serving motives versus public-serving motives) accounted for this difference. In Study 2 (N = 78), Study 3 (N = 51) we used experimental designs. Both experiments showed that organizations that communicated arguments incongruent with inferred organizational motives instigated less trust than organizations that communicated arguments congruent with inferred organizational motives. Study 3 additionally showed that communicating an incongruent, a congruent argument together diminished the negative effects of the incongruent argument. In both Study 2, Study 3 the effect of congruency on trust was mediated by perceived honesty of the organizations.

title: Cognitive, affective risk judgements related to climate change
authors: Sundblad, Eva-Lotta, Biel, Anders, Gärling, Tommy
keywords: CLIMATIC changes; CLIMATOLOGY; ACCLIMATIZATION; METEOROLOGY;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: A survey investigated risk judgements related to climate change. In order to understand which the important determinants of such risk judgements are, demographic factors, knowledge were assessed in a questionnaire answered by 621 Swedish residents. Demographic factors included gender, parenthood, type, level of education, age,, level of urbanization of the place of residence, while knowledge covered knowledge of state, causes,, consequences of climate change. Regression analyses showed that both cognitive risk judgements (of probability) of serious negative consequences, affective risk judgements (worry) were predicted by knowledge of causes, knowledge of consequences of climate change, in particular health consequences. Women were more worried than men but did not differ from men with respect to the cognitive risk judgements.

title: An exploration of place as a process: The case of Jackson Hole, WY
authors: Smaldone, David, Harris, Charles, Sanyal, Nick
keywords: place; meaning; life changes; physical setting; Environment; Experiences (Events); Environmental Psychology; Life Experiences;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: A variety of theoretical positions, frameworks have been advanced to account for how places become “places”—in other words, how places become meaningful. Most existing frameworks share the idea that a place is a complex concept, given life by people attaching meaning to a physical setting in a variety of ways. This paper explores how places evolve as ever-shifting points of meaning that mark changes in people's lives in response to a variety of influences. Data collected from in-depth personal interviews in, around Jackson, Wyoming, are used to explore the conceptualization of place as a process, rather than a static entity. Three key themes or dimensions that were frequently described by interviewees are examined: (1) life stage/course, (2) searching for a feeling,, (3) commitment to a place. Not only did some respondents describe what made places important to them (the components, such as social ties, or favorite activities), they also described how these attributes worked together to create, maintain place meanings over the course of their lives. During the interviews, it was noted that these dimensions, processes were expressed explicitly as well as implicitly.

title: Defining place attachment: A tripartite organizing framework
authors: Scannell, Leila, Gifford, Robert
keywords: Attachment Behavior; Environmental Psychology; Human; Person Environment Fit; place attachment;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Place attachment has been researched quite broadly,, so has been defined in a variety of ways. The various definitions of the concept are reviewed, synthesized into a three-dimensional, person–process–place organizing framework. The person dimension of place attachment refers to its individually or collectively determined meanings. The psychological dimension includes the affective, cognitive,, behavioral components of attachment. The place dimension emphasizes the place characteristics of attachment, including spatial level, specificity,, the prominence of social or physical elements. In addition, potential functions of place attachment are reviewed. The framework organizes related place attachment concepts, thus clarifies the term. The framework may also be used to stimulate new research, investigate multidimensionality, create operational definitions for quantitative studies, guide semi-structured interviews for qualitative studies,, assist in conflict resolution for successful land-use management.

title: An information–motivation–behavioral skills assessment of curbside recycling behavior
authors: Seacat, Jason D, Northrup, Denine
keywords: Recycling; Recycling behavior; Environment; Behavioral theory;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Despite annual increases in the amount of material solid waste (MSW) that is recycled in the United States, the overall amount of MSW generated continues to increase. In an effort to identify, test specific predictors of curbside recycling behavior, the current study adapted the empirically validated Information–Motivation–Behavioral Skills model (IMB), traditionally used to predict personal health behavior, to explain curbside recycling behavior. Using structured computer assisted telephone surveys with two random community samples; structural equation models indicated that the IMB model significantly predicted curbside recycling. Data from the current study provides specific information about critical psychosocial determinants of curbside recycling behavior, public policy implications.

title: Measuring knowledge of indoor environmental hazards
authors: Rosenthal, Sonny
keywords: Indoor environment; Science literacy; Knowledge; Scale development; Environmental risk; Environmental hazard;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: People spend most of their time indoors, where air pollution levels rival, often exceed those outdoors for a number of important pollutants. Yet, little is known about people’s knowledge of indoor environmental hazards. The purpose of the current study was to construct a measure of indoor environmental knowledge. A set of 78 true/false items were developed with input from a panel of experts. The set of items was truncated with traditional item analyses, resulting in a reliable set of 21 items (α = .79). Concurrent validity was established by a significant correlation between the indoor environmental knowledge (IEK) scale, an established measure of science literacy (r = 0.44, p < .001). Schema theory guided the assumption that the two measures should be related. Convergent validity was established by the significant regression of science literacy, formal education in science, math,, status as an engineering student on IEK scale score, accounting for 25\% of the variance in the IEK scale score. Future research avenues are proposed, limitations are discussed.

title: Development of a scale of perceived environmental annoyances in urban settings
authors: Robin, Monique, Annie Matheau-Police, Couty, Caroline
keywords: PSYCHOMETRICS; PSYCHOLOGY; MULTIDIMENSIONAL scaling; ENVIRONMENTAL sciences;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: The construction, validation of an original scale was pursued to measure perceived environmental annoyances in urban settings. This scale included all the potentially aversive situations encountered in the daily lives of city-dwellers. The answers of 926 French respondents to our initial 68-item scale were first analysed. Using statistical techniques, the number of items was reduced to 51 from which the factorial structure was extracted. Seven principal dimensions emerged: feelings of insecurity, inconveniences associated with using public transport, environmental annoyances, concerns for global ecology, lack of control over time related to using cars, incivilities associated with the sharing of public spaces between different users, lack of efficiency resulting from the density of the population,, an insecure, run-down living environment. We also examined these dimensions of perceived environmental annoyances in urban settings according to the sex, age, occupational category, geographical location of respondents. The validated multidimensional scale constitutes a promising instrument for urban research that could usefully be employed in the emerging field at the interface between health psychology, environmental psychology.

title: Residential satisfaction among aging people living in place
authors: Rioux, L, Werner, C
keywords: Elders' residential satisfaction; Neighborhood satisfaction; Well-being; Aging in place;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Residential satisfaction is a significant topic in environmental psychology yet there is little research on residential satisfaction among elders. This research aims to identify the cognitive structure of residential satisfaction of elderly persons living in their own dwellings, to identify demographic, psychological variables related to this residential satisfaction. One hundred, three participants, ranging in age from 72 to 86 years old, living at home in the central France, answered (a) a purpose-developed questionnaire to measure their residential satisfaction, (b) an environmental quality questionnaire aimed at evaluating both the physical, social environments,, (c) several psychological variables including: the ESV, a French adaptation of the Satisfaction with Life Scale which examines the general well-being of aging people;, three single well-being items assessing financial well-being, perceived health,, perception of oneself as active. The results indicated that in this sample, residential satisfaction corresponds to a four-dimension structure organized by physical location rather than psychological or behavioral aspects. The four components were the local area, access to services, relations with neighbors,, the home itself. Satisfaction with each component was related to different predictors, supporting the idea that elders hold complex, nuanced views of their homes, neighborhoods.

title: Place-identity: Physical world socialization of the self
authors: Proshansky, Harold M, Fabian, Abbe K, Kaminoff, Robert
keywords: place-identity as cognitions of physical settings, development of self identity; Cognitive Maps; Environmental Psychology; Personality Development; Self Concept;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Theorized that place-identity is a cluster of positively, negatively valenced cognitions of physical settings. The substantive, valuative natures of these cognitions help to define who, of what value the individual is both to him/herself, in terms of how he/she thinks others view him/her. Three factors are seen as underlying the influence of physical settings on the development of place-identity in the individual: the physical settings of the home, school,, neighborhood. It is in the home, school,, neighborhood settings that the child learns some of his/her most significant social roles (e.g., sex, peer-group membership, ethnic group membership). (47 ref) (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2008 APA, all rights reserved)

title: Assessment of outdoor school environments, physical activity in Ankara's primary schools
authors: Ozdemir, Aydin, Yilmaz, Oguz
keywords: Schoolyard; Physical activity; Obesity; Landscape design; Ankara;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Outdoor school environments are sites for play, physical activity for many children,, shortcomings within these environments are considered significant factors that contribute to children's inactive lifestyles, high levels of childhood obesity. This study explores the associations between the physical characteristics of schoolyards, the physical activity of third, fourth year students in five Turkish primary schools. Data were collected through multiple methods, including behavior mapping of student activities during recess, physical assessments of schoolyards,, interviews with students, teachers, administrations. The findings show similarities in the landscape features, physical qualities of schoolyards, particularly in the types of play, activities in which students engage. Results indicated that active students who walk to, from schools have lower body mass index (BMI) values than passive students,, students in schools with larger yards have lower BMI values. Most of the students prefer spacious, vegetated yards. A major concern is the crowdedness of the yards during recess that limit children's activity. Schoolyards with advanced landscape features are preferred more,, this in turn affects students’ positive satisfaction. Outdoor school environments have a correlation to health outcomes, should be designed to promote more activity. Improving the physical, landscape qualities of the public schoolyards should be the primary concern of the designers in order to increase awareness of natural environment, more important, increase the health of children.

title: The dual-process of reactive, intentional decision-making involved in eco-friendly behavior
authors: Ohtomo, Shoji, Hirose, Yukio
keywords: DECISION making; PROBLEM solving; PROTOTYPES, Engineering; DETERMINANTS;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: We extended the prototype model Gibbons, Gerrard to examine the disparity between professed environmental concerns, behavior. Our model assumed that there are two decision processes: a reactive process involving unintentional decision-making based on situational factors,, an intentional process involving goal-oriented decision-making based on attitudinal factors. A questionnaire about recycling behavior was completed by 206 Japanese undergraduate students. The results indicated that the prototype image, descriptive norm were determinants of the reactive process to accept eco-unfriendly behavior. In contrast, environmental concern, the injunctive norm were determinants of the intentional process to promote eco-friendly behavior. Our model suggests that eco-friendly behavior may be inhibited or promoted depending upon whether the reactive process or the intentional process is more salient.

title: Differences in rural landscape perceptions, preferences between farmers, naturalists
authors: Natori, Yoji, Chenoweth, Richard
keywords: Semantic differential; Land use; Group difference; Rice paddy; Woodland;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: A long history of human–nature interactions mediated by agriculture, resulted in high biodiversity in Japanese rural landscapes. This diversity faces drastic decline due to the changes following the socioeconomic circumstances regarding agriculture. Rural conservation will require cooperation among major stakeholders,, knowing how preferences for, perceptions of rural landscapes differ among them can help crafting, implementing effective conservation measures. This study investigated how perceptions of rural landscapes in the Arai-Keinan region, Niigata, Japan differ among people having very different relationships to them. In a photograph-based semantic differential survey, farmers, naturalists, major stakeholders in rural conservation, rated both rice paddy, woodland landscapes. In determining preferences for rice paddy landscapes, perceptions of stewardship, openness were significantly more important for farmers, whereas those of naturalness, biodiversity were significantly more important for naturalists. Such group differences were not found for woodland landscapes. Analysis of perceptions for landscape changes suggested that farmers may have higher normative criteria for rural landscapes than naturalists. Group preferences for intensified rice paddies on sloped topography may conflict,, any rural conservation planning effort should carefully consider that farmers, naturalists consider different aspects of landscapes as important.

title: People living in ageing buildings: Their quality of life, sense of belonging
authors: Ng, Sik Hung, Kam, Ping Kwong, Pong, Raymond W M
keywords: Environmental Psychology; Housing; Person Environment Fit; Quality of Life; Human; Male; Female; Hong Kong; aging buildings; environmental factors; dwelling quality; sense of belonging; Life Satisfaction Index Form;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: The first objective of this study is to develop measures of housing-related environmental factors (quality of dwelling, neighbours, community), place belonging. Another objective is to test the impacts of housing-related environmental factors on quality of life (QoL), place belonging. Interview data were collected from 576 residents in six districts that had been designated for demolition as part of a major urban renewal programme in Hong Kong. The findings showed that the QoL measures (life satisfaction, family life, health) were related weakly (or not at all) to various demographic, socio-economic factors. By contrast, the environmental factors, when added to the regression equations, significantly raised the variance explained. For place belonging, the environmental factors closest to the home of the residents (i.e. quality of dwelling, neighbours) exerted a greater influence than the more distal factor (i.e. the wider community). The overall findings demonstrated the relevance of housing to two issues—QoL, place belonging—that are important topics in environmental social psychology relating to urban renewal.

title: Form, function in public buildings
authors: Nasar, Jack L, Stamps, III, Arthur E, Hanyu, Kazunori
keywords: PUBLIC administration; PUBLIC works; CONTINGENCY tables; MATHEMATICAL statistics;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: The American architect Louis Sullivan once proclaimed “Form follows function.” We tested this maxim by obtaining random samples of four types of buildings, obtaining samples from three countries of respondents unacquainted with the buildings sampled,, asking the respondents to guess which function went with which building. If form follows function, it would enhance legibility, presumably improving wayfinding, the quality of experience. χ2 analyses of the contingency tables indicated that form had a small effect on perceived function. Thus, for the building types sampled, form did not follow function.

title: Effects of labelled meaning on the affective quality of housing scenes
authors: Nasar, Jack L, Julian, David
keywords: Environmental Attitudes; Housing; Labeling; Urban Environments; Emotional Responses; Imagination;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: A series of studies examined the effects of labelled meaning on affective response to housing scenes. Students at Ohio State University assessed their feelings towards imagined housing (public or private), cities (Memphis, Houston, San Francisco). Expected differences in the affective quality were found. Responses to color photographs of specific housing scenes labelled as either private condominiums or public housing were obtained. Differences in scene-affect as a function of labelled meaning were found. Responses to housing scenes labelled as located in either Memphis, Houston or San Francisco revealed no differences in scene-affect as a function of label meaning. This latter finding was confirmed in a non-repeated measure examination. Differences in the fittingness, potency or relevance of the information provided may account for the pattern of findings.

title: Towards a developmental theory of place attachment
authors: Morgan, Paul
keywords: Attachment Behavior; Childhood Development; Early Experience; Human; Male; Female; developmental theory; place attachment; child development; childhood experiences;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Place theory offers no explanation of the developmental processes by which place attachment arises. Drawing on recent findings in human attachment theory, this study offers a developmental model of the process by which place attachment emerges from a childhood place experience. A pattern of positively affected experiences of place in childhood are generalised into an unconscious internal working model of place which manifests subjectively as a long-term positively affected bond to place known as place attachment. Qualitative analysis of adult remembrance of childhood place experience provides support for this model, finds important parallels in the developmental processes underpinning place attachment, human attachment as well as some differences.

title: Visual preferences of elderly public housing residents: Residential street scenes
authors: Nasar, J
abstract: Multiple regression predictors related judged visual attributes of housing exteriors to evaluative responses by 56 elderly persons living in public housing in 2 cities. In one city, the safety, composite preference evaluations of the 30 neighborhoods portrayed in photographs were found inversely related to both the dilapidation, diversity of the street scenes. In the other city, the same evaluations were found related to the dullness, openness of the street scenes. In both cases, the responses predicted by the multiple regression equations for the sample in one city showed significant correlations with the obtained evaluative responses by the sample in the other city. However, the equations with dilapidation, diversity were the better predictors. (26 ref) (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved)

title: Place attachment, flood preparedness
authors: Mishra, Sasmita, Mazumdar, Sanjoy, Suar, Damodar
keywords: Place attachment; Flood preparedness; Natural disaster preparedness; Emotional connections to place; Orissa, India;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Does place attachment, the consequent emotional connections, ties that people have with environments affect their preparedness for natural disasters, such as floods? This study took up this research question for the understudied geographical region of Orissa, India. In particular, investigation focused on three kinds of place attachment, viz. economic, genealogical,, religious. Contextualized scales for place attachment, flood preparedness were developed for a survey. Data were collected from 300 residents in flood prone areas. Validity, reliability of the scales were established. Overall, place attachment was found to significantly influence flood preparedness. Hierarchical regression analysis was performed to determine whether the three factors of place attachment influence flood preparedness. Controlling for confounding effects of age, family type, regression analysis revealed that people having genealogical, economic place attachment prepared for floods, but those with religious place attachment did not prepare for floods. The implications of these findings for future studies are described.

title: Children's neighborhood place as a psychological, behavioral domain
authors: Min, Byungho, Lee, Jongmin
keywords: Behavior; Childhood Development; Environment; Neighborhoods; Social Interaction; Psychology; Human; Male; Female; South Korea; children's neighborhood place; environmental attributes; psychological domain; behavioral domain; affordances;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Interviews of 91 children living in a large high-rise, high-density planned neighborhood of 5277 families reveal that children find most of their psychologically valued settings within the neighborhood outdoor spaces such as designated play areas, developed parks. They are aware of differences in experience between such valued ‘places’, other ‘spaces’. They choose the places because such places offer some key environmental attributes—spatial, physical,, social—that support behaviors that children want to engage in. Due to these attributes, behaviors in places are different from behaviors in other spaces, with the former being more purposive, social, creative,, dependent on particular affordances of the setting. This can be confirmed in a follow-up behavioral analysis of three pairs of most popular places, their counterpart settings. This observational analysis shows that settings children mention to be important to them are utilized more often (about twice as much) than their counterparts, showing a variety of behaviors, incorporating more intentional activities (as opposed to transient, short-lived ones), encouraging group behaviors (as opposed to single-person activities),, providing children with a sense of their own territorial play area. The study demonstrates that in children's neighborhood environment, emergence of such important places is related to use pattern, there are some key attributes, core behaviors greatly contributing to children's place experience.

title: The measurement of ‘rootedness’, the prediction of attachment to home-towns in college students
authors: McAndrew, Francis T
keywords: development \& cross validation of scale to measure rootedness, prediction of attachment to home towns, college students; Attachment Behavior; Environmental Attitudes; Home Environment; Likert Scales; Test Construction; Prediction;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: A 10-item questionnaire measuring ‘rootedness’ was developed using a sample of 134 undergraduates at a large state university. In a second study, the questionnaire was cross-validated with a sample of 126 undergraduates drawn from two other institutions. The questionnaire consists of two subscales based on factors called ‘Desire for Change’, ‘Home/Family Satisfaction’. In both samples, the scales successfully predicted place-relevant behavior, feelings such as the frequency of homesickness, the intention to return to one's home town following graduation, the frequency of visits from friends back home,, subscriptions to home-town newspapers. The results suggest that place attachment can be thought of as a quantifiable individual difference which might be used to predict the difficulty individuals will experience following relocation.

title: Environmental personalization, elementary school children's self-esteem
authors: Maxwell, Lorraine E, Chmielewski, Emily J
keywords: CLASSROOM environment; KINDERGARTEN; PHYSICAL environment; SELF-esteem;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Prior research indicates that the physical classroom environment has the potential to affect children's behaviors, academic performance,, cognitive development. However, less is understood about the effect on the socio-emotional development of children. This study investigates the potential role of one aspect of the classroom's physical environment, personalization displays, on children's self-esteem. The study employed a classroom intervention in a quasi-experiment to examine the effects of increasing environmental personalization on children's self-esteem. Thirty-eight kindergarteners, first graders in six classrooms of two elementary schools in a rural community of a north-eastern state were assessed on pretests, post-tests of the Self-Esteem Index (SEI) scale, the Children's Inventory of Self-Esteem (CISE) scale. The findings were mixed but encouraging. On both measures of self-esteem, there was a significant positive effect of classroom personalization for first graders. However, for kindergarteners there was a significant positive effect for only one measure, the CISE. Although there are limitations with the study design, the findings suggest that young children's self-esteem may be influenced, enhanced by specific aspects of the classroom's physical environment.

title: Disaster preparedness, perception of flood risk: A study in an alpine valley in Italy
authors: Miceli, Renato, Sotgiu, Igor, Settanni, Michele
keywords: EMERGENCY management; ITALY; NATURAL disasters; RISK perception;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Italy is a country highly vulnerable to floods, landslides. The present study aims to investigate disaster preparedness, perception of flood risk in a group of people living in an alpine valley in the north of Italy. Four hundred seven adult residents in nine communities exposed to hydrogeological risk were interviewed by using a structured questionnaire. Participants were asked about the adoption of a set of protective behaviors that can prevent negative consequences of floods. Perception of flood risk was assessed by means of a one-dimensional scale that was developed, validated by the authors. Items included in this scale asked participants to estimate likelihood of occurrence of different flood consequences, to express feelings of worry associated to them. Socio-demographic, experiential information on respondents were also collected. Overall, results showed that most of respondents were fairly well prepared to deal with a future flood disaster. Correlational, regression analyses indicated that disaster preparedness was positively associated with risk perception. In accordance with literature, there was not a significant relation between likelihood judgments, adoption of protective behaviors, while feelings of worry were associated with disaster preparedness. Authors interpret their results in relation to the socio-environmental characteristics of the studied communities. Theoretical, empirical, practical implications of the findings are also discussed.

title: Image of neighborhood, self-image, sense of community
authors: Mannarini, Terri, Tartaglia, Stefano, Fedi, Angela, Greganti, Katiuscia
keywords: Communities; Neighborhoods; Self Concept; Human; Male; Female; Italy; image of neighborhood; self-image; sense of community; Italian Sense of Community Scale;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: The present study was carried out on a sample of residents of three Italian cities (N=1031) to pursue two aims: (a) to explore the relationship between the images of the community of residence, sense of community,, (b) to investigate the relationship between self, neighborhood images. In order to identify neighborhood, self-image, free associations of words to the statements “my neighborhood is”, “I am” underwent a cluster analysis; then a correspondence analysis between these two types of representations, the sense of community level was performed.Results showed a relationship between the subjective image of the neighborhood, sense of community, but did not point out a clear relation between self, neighborhood images. Theoretical, empirical implications are discussed.

title: Place attachment, place identity,, place memory: Restoring the forgotten city past
authors: Lewicka, Maria
keywords: Ethnic bias; Place attachment; Place identity; Place memory; Social memory;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: This paper investigates collective memory in inhabitants of two twin cities, Lviv (Ukraine, previously Lwów, Poland), Wrocław (Poland, previously Breslau, Germany). Due to territorial changes in Eastern, Central Europe after World War II, the two cities changed their state belonging and—consequently—their populations. This study focused on memory of residence place, on its relationship with place identity, place attachment.A sample of 200 participants from three districts of Lviv, 301 participants from four districts of Wrocław were investigated on a number of issues, including reported place identity (city district, city, country region, nation, Europe, world, human being), place attachment (apartment, house, neighborhood, city district, city), place memory (memory of the city, the city district, the street,, the house). Collective memory showed a powerful ethnic bias, equally strong in both cities, but with different underlying mechanisms: predictors of the bias were national identity in Lviv, demographic variables (age), lack of place identity in Wrocław. Place (city) was constructed as national symbol in Lviv,, as an autonomous entity in Wrocław. Some evidence was also obtained that the degree to which place attachment is associated with the higher-order (national) or lower-order (local) identity predicts the amount of ethnic bias in perceptions of the pre-war past of the two cities. The findings are interpreted within the dual-process models of perception, here applied to perception of places.

title: Rating scale measures of restorative components of environments
authors: Laumann, Karin, Gärling, Tommy, Stormark, Kjell Morten
keywords: test development; factor analysis; rating scale measures; restorative components of environments; Environmental Attitudes; Rating Scales; Test Construction; Well Being; Person Environment Fit;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Two studies were conducted with the aim of developing a set of rating scale measures of restorative components of environments. In Study 1, 238 Norwegian undergraduates acting as subjects imagined themselves to be either in a nature environment or a city environment which they rated on unipolar scales intended to describe how they experienced the environments. In Study 2 another sample of 157 subjects recruited from the same population of Norwegian undergraduates viewed videos of a forest, park, sea area, city,, a snowy mountain, imagining themselves to be in these environments while performing ratings on the same scales. In both studies factor analyses yielded results in agreement with a theory proposed by Kaplan, Kaplan (1989). However, the being away factor posited by the theory was split into two factors, one with high loadings on rating scales tapping being physically away, the other with high loadings on rating scales tapping being psychologically away. The remaining three factors were defined by rating scales tapping extent, fascination,, compatibility, respectively. Composite measures of the factors had acceptable reliability. Furthermore, as predicted, environments with nature elements generally scored higher than city environments on all measures. Compatibility, fascination predicted preference ratings of the environments, whereas escape, compatibility predicted selfratings of relaxation.

title: Stability of self-reported favourite places, place attachment over a 10-month period
authors: Korpela, Kalevi M, Ylén, Matti, Tyrväinen, Liisa, Silvennoinen, Harri
keywords: Credibility; Evaluation; Self Regulation; Urban Environments; Human; Male; Female; Finland; place selection stability; favorite places; place attachment; place selection reliability; evaluations;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: We investigated the reliability, stability of favourite place selections, evaluations of place attachment over a 10-month period. A simple random sample of 1273 respondents representative of the population of the two largest cities in Finland completed a mailed questionnaire. Reliability data was obtained in a second questionnaire (N = 427). We obtained five main favourite place types which were extensively managed natural settings (mainly urban woodlands), urban green spaces (mostly parks), waterside environments, exercise, activity/hobby areas,, indoor, outdoor urban areas. Sixty-four percent of the respondents in the second survey selected the same main favourite place type as 10 months earlier, which is more than what might be expected by chance. Extensively managed natural settings (mainly urban woodlands), waterside environments were reselected most often. Indoor, outdoor urban favourite places had the lowest stability. We found evidence of people being more consistent in their attachment to natural favourite places than to urban favourite places. The findings lend further credence, credibility to earlier results concerning self-regulation, restorative experiences in favourite places.

title: Wayfinding with a GPS-based mobile navigation system: A comparison with maps, direct experience
authors: Ishikawa, Toru, Fujiwara, Hiromichi, Imai, Osamu, Okabe, Atsuyuki
keywords: GLOBAL Positioning System; MAPS; TRAILS; TRAVEL;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of a Global Positioning System (GPS)-based mobile navigation system in comparison to paper maps, direct experience of routes, by focusing on the user's wayfinding behavior, acquired spatial knowledge. Based on information received from one of these three media, participants walked six routes finding the way to goals. Results showed that GPS users traveled longer distances, made more stops during the walk than map users, direct-experience participants. Also, GPS users traveled more slowly, made larger direction errors, drew sketch maps with poorer topological accuracy,, rated wayfinding tasks as more difficult than direct-experience participants. Characteristics of navigation with these three learning media, possible reasons for the ineffectiveness of the GPS-based navigation system are discussed.

title: Relocation, privacy regulation: A cross-cultural analysis
authors: Harris, P, Werner, Carol M, Brown, B, Ingebritsen, Dave
keywords: Asians; Foreign Students; Privacy; Attachment Behavior; College Students; Quality of Life;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Abstract Although privacy needs may be universal, the exact mechanisms used to regulate privacy can vary considerably from culture to culture. Consequently, when individuals relocate across cultures, privacy regulation with new neighbours may involve an incongruity between previously-learned privacy mechanisms, those prescribed by the new culture of residence. These disruptions in ability to regulate privacy can be particularly problematic given that effective regulation may relate to place attachment, a sense of well-being. Survey responses made by Asian, American students in the U.S.A. support this hypothesis. Compared to U.S.A. students, Asians had more difficulty establishing contacts with their new neighbours. However, as interaction with family within the home is an 'intra-cultural' phenomenon, these students did not have difficulty regulating privacy with family. The possible universal importance of privacy regulation was supported for both U.S.A., Asian students in that effective regulation was related to place attachment, this attachment was related to a subjective sense of well-being.

title: Privacy regulation, place attachment : Predicting attachments to a student family housing facility
authors: Harris, P, Brown, B, Werner, Carol M
keywords: privacy regulation \& place attachment in the home, 19-69 yr old student family apartment residents; Home Environment; Models; Privacy;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Abstract Although similar processes, functions have been proposed for privacy regulation, place attachment, little theoretical or empirical work encompasses both constructs. In the present study, a theoretical model relates privacy regulation to place attachment in the home. According to this model, the home setting may either facilitate or inhibit privacy regulation with family. When regulation is facilitated, family functioning, feelings of control should be enhanced, promoting attachments to the home. Questionnaire data from student family apartment residents supported this model. Residents who reported greater ease in regulating privacy with family also reported greater apartment attachment. Analyses suggested that this relationship was mediated by family functioning, feelings of control. Similar relationships were found for three different types of attachment. By bridging across concepts often treated separately, the model supported in this study suggests new directions for theoretical, empirical study,, new applications for housing policy, design.

title: Sense of place in developmental context
authors: Hay, Robert
keywords: residential status \& developmental age stage \& adult pair bond \& development of sense of place, 15-70+ yr olds, New Zealand; Age Differences; Developmental Stages; Geography; Living Arrangements; Sociocultural Factors;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Sense of place differs from place attachment by considering the social, geographical context of place bonds, the sensing of places, such as aesthetics, a feeling of dwelling. Insider status, local ancestry are important toward the development of a more rooted sense of place. Three contexts are used to examine the development of sense of place: residential status in the place (superficial, partial, personal, ancestral,, cultural senses of place); age stage, as in development across the life cycle, using a psychodynamic model (after Erikson, Vaillant);, development of the adult pair bond, most often in marriage. Being raised in the place affected feelings of rootedness, particularly for Maori peoples who have ties to tribal territory. Interactions were found among place, pair bonds,, multigenerational patterns were noted for ancestral, cultural senses of place, with sense of place styles passed from parent to child. Modern society, due especially to high levels of residential mobility, tends to develop more of a partial or personal sense of place among its members. Sequential stages in the development of a sense of place were most evident among those who were raised in the place, spent most of their lives there: embryonic (childhood to adolescent); commitment (early to mid adulthood);, culmination (mid adulthood to old age). These became apparent in phenomenological, statistical analyses of responses from 270 adult residents of Banks Peninsula, New Zealand, of both Maori, European descent. Additional interviews were conducted with 80 adult out-migrants from the Peninsula; brief surveys were also done of tourists, long-term campers, holiday home owners,, resident school children on Banks Peninsula. Models of place attachment need to be reconsidered, as does the value of developing a sense of place based more on ancestral, cultural connections. Such a sense of place is considered to be of benefit to individuals, to modern society.@ 1998 Academic Press

title: At home on the road? Can drivers’ relationships with their cars be associated with territoriality?
authors: Fraine, Graham, Smith, Sandy G, Zinkiewicz, Lucy, Chapman, Rebekah, Sheehan, Mary
keywords: HUMAN territoriality; CHILDREN \& adults; TERRITORIALITY (Zoology); SPATIAL behavior in animals;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: The current research explores the relationship between people, their cars within the framework of Altman's theory of human territoriality. It further develops the research of Sandqvist by examining the descriptions given by people with differing ownership, uses of their cars, exploring the congruence between these, the characteristics used to describe human territories. Thirteen focus groups were held with young drivers between the ages of 18, 25 years, drivers over the age of 25 who are parents of pre-license age children, drivers over the age of 25 who do not regularly transport children,, drivers of work vehicles. Analyses of discussions revealed that drivers’ descriptions of the relationship with their car could be matched with Brown, Altman's descriptions of territory types. However, variations existed both between, within individuals as to the application of the labels ‘primary’, ‘secondary’, ‘public’ territory to the car. Implications for the understanding of road user behaviour, the further development of theory on the car as a place or an object in terms of territoriality are discussed.

title: Walking routes to school in new urban, suburban neighborhoods: An environmental walkability analysis of blocks, routes
authors: Gallimore, Jonathan M, Brown, Barbara B, Werner, Carol M
keywords: Walkability; Urban design; New urbanism; Environmental perceptions; Walk to school;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: We assessed environmental, perceptual correlates of walking, walkability for fifth graders from three communities attending two schools: A new urban/LEED-ND pilot community, mixed,, standard suburban community. Irvine-Minnesota Inventory (IMI) walkability audits showed that new urban blocks provided more traffic safety, pleasurability, crime safety, density,, diversity. New urban routes offered greater traffic safety, accessibility, pleasurability, crime safety,, diversity, but suburban routes had greater housing density, net of controls (parental education, rooms in the home, home ownership, parent preference for child to walk to school). Parents, children perceived new urban routes to be more walkable, children walked more when they lived on more walkable routes. The suburban hierarchical street design exposed children to varied traffic safety conditions by funneling their walks from cul-de-sacs to arterials. The new urban routes to a centrally located school passed by pleasant open spaces, suggesting how community organization can create better walking conditions.

title: Relationships between street characteristics, perceived attractiveness for walking reported by elderly people
authors: Borst, Hieronymus C, Miedema, Henk M E, de Vries, Sanne I, Graham, Jamie M A, van Dongen, Jef E F
keywords: Elderly people; Pedestrians; Perceived attractiveness; Physical environment; Walking;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: Walking is important for the health of elderly people. Previous studies have found a relationship between neighbourhood characteristics, physical activity, related health aspects. The multivariate linear regression model presented here describes the relationships between the perceived attractiveness of streets for walking along, (physical) street characteristics. Two hundred, eighty-eight independently living elderly people (between 55, 80 years old) participated in the study. Street characteristics were assessed along homogeneous street subsections defined as ‘links’. Positively related to perceived attractiveness of links were the following street characteristics: slopes and/or stairs, zebra crossings, trees along the route, front gardens, bus, tram stops, shops, business buildings, catering establishments, passing through parks or the city centre,, traffic volume. Litter on the street, high-rise buildings,, neighbourhood density of dwellings were negatively related to perceived link attractiveness. Overall, the results suggest that three main aspects affect perceived attractiveness of streets for walking, namely tidiness of the street, its scenic value, the presence of activity or other people along the street. The results are discussed within the context of these three aspects.

title: Differentiation of determinants of low-cost, high-cost recycling
authors: Andersson, Maria, von Borgstede, Chris
keywords: Recycling; Low-cost hypothesis; Social norms; Personal norms;jep\_org;J Environ Psychol
abstract: The bulk of research on recycling has been devoted to disentangling factors that affect it. Based on the low-cost hypothesis, we suggest that psychological factors differentially influence behaviors that are relatively less costly to perform compared to behaviors that are more costly to perform. Recycling has often been viewed as low-cost behavior, neglecting that recycling in different waste categories may vary in cost. The aim of the present study was to apply, extend the low-cost hypothesis by investigating whether beliefs about environmental consequences, knowledge,, norms differentially affect low-cost, high-cost recycling. A survey of 418 participants showed that knowledge, social norms,, personal norms were related to both low-cost, high-cost recycling, but the relation was significantly stronger for high-cost recycling. Personal norms partially mediated procedural knowledge, social norms in both low-cost, high-cost recycling. The findings emphasize the need to regard recycling as a multiform behavior, to analyse its determinants separately for different waste categories.

title: The persuasive effects of message framing in organ donation: The mediating role of psychological reactance
authors: Reinhart, Amber Marie, Marshall, Heather M, Feeley, Thomas Hugh, Tutzauer, Frank
abstract: The effects of message framing on reactions to campaign messages promoting organ donation were examined in three experiments. It was predicted that gain-framed messages would produce more positive reactions toward organ, tissue donation. In Study 1, students (N=189) responded to either a gain-framed or loss-framed message about organ donation. Study 2 (N=318), Study 3 (N=433) examined the role of psychological reactance as a mediator between framing, reactions. Results indicated an effect for framing across the three studies—specifically, students reading a gain-framed message reported more favorable reactions toward the scripted message, lower psychological reactance. Psychological reactance, perceived manipulative intent were found to mediate the relationship between framing, message reactions.

title: Self-efficacy expectancy, outcome expectancy,, outcome value: Relative effects on behavioral intentions
authors: Maddux, James E, Norton, Larry W, Stoltenberg, Cal D
keywords: Behavior; Expectations; Prediction; Self Efficacy; Human; behavioral Intention;org;315\_介入実験\_情報提示
abstract: Using a factorial experiment, a persuasive communications paradigm, we examined the relative contributions of self-efficacy expectancy, outcome expectancy,, outcome value (importance) in influencing, predicting behavioral intentions. Outcome expectancy was manipulated independent of self-efficacy expectancy, had a main effect on behavioral intentions, but self-efficacy expectancy failed to produce a main effect on intentions. The outcome-value manipulation also had a main effect on intentions, although problems with the manipulation check made interpretations of this effect problematic. Correlational data revealed that assessments of self-efficacy expectancy, outcome expectancy,, outcome value were all significant, roughly equivalent predictors of intentions. Each component also significantly contributed to the other two components combined in the prediction of behavioral intentions.

title: The persuasive effects of audiovisual PSAs to promote organ donation: The mediating role of psychological reactance
authors: LaVail, Katherine Hart, Anker, Ashley E, Reinhart, Amber, Feeley, Thomas Hugh
abstract: The content, effects of organ donation public service announcements (PSAs) were analyzed in 2 studies. Study 1 identified 17 30-second PSAs in the public domain, coded them for content using Marwell, Schmitt's (1967) persuasive message typology. Common codes identified included liking, positive self-feeling, altruism,, moral appeal. Study 2 measured undergraduate students' evaluations of persuasive strategies, psychological reactance,, message reactions. Results indicated that PSAs were not perceived differently on the basis of donor status or message condition. However, students' perceptions of persuasive strategies were influential based on donor status. For non-donors, psychological reactance fully mediated the relationship between perceptions of impersonal commitments strategies, message reactions, such that increased psychological reactance was associated with reduced message reactions. For donors, psychological reactance, perceptions of persuasive strategies had no effect on message reactions. Results are discussed in the context of campaign development.

title: Ineffectiveness of threat appeals about drinking, driving
authors: Kohn, Paul M, Goodstadt, Michael S, Cook, Gaynoll M, Sheppard, Margaret, Chan, Godwin
keywords: Alcohol Drinking Patterns; Driving Behavior; High School Students; Knowledge Level; Student Attitudes; Films; Threat;org;315\_介入実験\_情報提示
abstract: Four groups of high school students (total N = 441) were each exposed to one of the following films: A High-Threat, Medium-Threat, or Low-Threat appeal about impaired driving; or an irrelevant Control film. The threatening films evoked varying degrees of general upset (anxiety, depression, loss of pleasure,, disgust) rather than just fear. All three experimental groups outscored control subjects on an immediate posttest measure of knowledge about drinking, driving; however, this advantage dissipated by the delayed posttest, six months later. The high-, low-threat films actually evoked more permissive attitudes to impaired driving than the control film did on the immediate posttest; however, no attitudinal differences among treatments appeared on the delayed posttest. The experimental films also failed to affect self-reports of impaired-driving frequency over the six months between the two posttests. Possible reasons were suggested for the evident ineffectiveness of the threat appeals,, possible issues for further investigation were identified.

title: Criminal victimization in contemporary China: a review of the evidence, challenges for future research
authors: Zhuo, Yue, Messner, Steven F, Zhang, Lening
keywords: VICTIMS of crimes; CRIMINAL statistics; SOCIAL policy; CRIMINOLOGICAL research; SOCIAL change; CHINA -- Social conditions -- 2000-; CHINA;10\_英語の研究
abstract: The rapid economic growth in China over recent decades has been accompanied by higher levels of crime, but there have been few studies of the Chinese experience of criminal victimization. A recent victimization survey of a representative sample of households in Tianjin represents a major effort to fill this gap in the literature. The present paper reviews the research based on the Tianjin survey along with other studies of crime, criminal victimization in China that have been published since 1990. We summarize the major findings, discuss the theoretical perspectives, methodological strategies that have been applied, identify the limitations of the research to date,, offer suggestions for future research. title: 女性・子供を対象とした脅威事案に関する近接反復被害仮説の検証 髙橋あい(筑波大学システム情報工学研究科) 雨宮 護(筑波大学システム情報系社会工学域) 島田貴仁(科学警察研究所犯罪行動科学部)
authors: 高橋, あ い, 雨宮, 護
abstract: キーワード：女性・子供，脅威事案，近接反復被害 背景と目的 犯罪の近接反復被害とは、 最初の犯罪の発生後、 時間的、距離的に近い時(地)点で、次の犯罪が 発生しやすくなる現象を指す。警察では、女性や 子供といった犯罪弱者に対するちかんや公然わ いせつ等の脅威事案の通報を、 メール配信や web 等で住民に迅速に情報共有しており、 対策にあた りこの仮説が成立することが前提とされている。 しかし、 ちかんや公然わいせつ等に対する近接反 復被害の仮説は実証されていない。本研究では、 ちかんや公然わいせつ等の脅威事案の種類別に、 近接反復被害仮説を検証する。 方法 2014～16 年において警視庁が通報を受けた脅 威事案(ちかん、つきまとい、のぞき、盗撮、公 然わいせつ、声かけ、卑わい言動、不審者)のう ち、公共空間で発生し、番地・号レベルの位置情 報を持つ 16,890 件を分析する。被害者の年齢が 13 歳以上の女性を大人、13 歳未満の男女を子供 と分類した上で分析を行う。データは「警視庁子 ども・女性の安全対策に関する有識者研究会」の もとで供与されたものである。 分析では、実際の事案発生状況(実測値)と、 各事案が独立して発生したと仮定して作成した 標本値を比較する(菊池ら，2009) 。具体的には 以下の通り。①実測値の計算：時間変数と距離変 数が含まれた事案データを 1 件抽出し、 残りの事 案データとの時間差、距離を計算する。これを全 ての事案データについて行い、 任意の時間差と距 離を閾値とするクロス集計表を作成する。 ②標本 値の計算：事案の発生時間をランダムに入れ換え、 ①を行う。これを 999 回繰り返す。③リスクの算 出：クロス表の各セルに含まれる実測値の頻度と、 標本値の頻度(平均値)の比を取り、独立と比較 して上昇したリスク(knox 比)を求める。 結果 大人・子供へのちかん・公然わいせつと、子供 への声かけにおいて近接反復被害が確認された。 大人へのちかんでは、 最初の犯罪が発生してか ら 250m 圏内で、14 日以内で約 1.5 倍、1 ヶ月以 内 で 約 1.4 倍 の リ ス ク の 上 昇 が 確 認 さ れ た (Figure 1) 。大人への公然わいせつでも同様に、 250m 圏内で 1 ヶ月程、1.3～1.4 倍のリスクの上 昇がみられた。 子供へのちかん、公然わいせつ、声かけでは、 いずれも、 大人よりリスクの上昇幅が大きかった。 ちかんでは、最初の事案発生後 500m 圏内、1 ヶ 月以内でリスクが約 4.0 倍となった。公然わいせ つでは、1km 圏内、7 日以内で約 3.0 倍と比較的 近い時間範囲でのリスクの上昇が確認された。 声 かけでは、500m 圏内、14 日以内で 4.8～6.2 倍の リスクの上昇がみられた。 以上より、女性・子供を対象とする脅威事案に は近接反復被害の傾向が認められた。しかし、具 体的にリスクが高まる時間的・距離的範囲は事案 ごとに異なっていた。対策にあたっては、こうし た違いを考慮する必要があると考えられる。 Figure 1. 大人を対象とした「ちかん」の上昇リスク (実測値と標本値との比。色は数値の大きさに対応。) 引用文献 菊池城治・⾬宮護・島⽥貴仁・⿑藤知範・原⽥豊(2009). 声かけなどの不審者遭遇情報と性犯罪の時空間的近接 性の分析, 犯罪社会学研究, 34, 151-163. title: Analyzing Sex Crime Victimization Risk : Who, When,, Where is Riskiest?
authors: 雨宮護, 大山智也, 島田貴仁
abstract: In this study, sex crime victimization risks for victim age groups, hours at which they occurred,, places at which they occurred were calculated using the ambient population of women estimated from person trip survey data. From the analysis of sex crimes reported in Tokyo from 2011 to 2016, the following conclusions were derived. First, while the highest number of sex crimes occurs to victims aged 20 to 24, the age group at greatest risk is 20 to 24 too. Second, the hour of greatest risk, the hour of the highest number of crimes are not coincident. The hour of greatest risk follows the hour of the highest number of crimes. Finally, places with the greatest risk for sex crimes are distributed outside areas considered high-crime places. 性犯罪、曝露人口、被害リスク、動的人口、パーソントリップ調査、人の流れデータ 1. はじめに 犯罪は特定の場所や時間帯に集中して起こる事象である．そ うした場所や時間帯を同定することは， 様々な防犯資源の効率的 な配分や， 人々への適切な注意喚起をするうえで重要である． こ うした前提から，これまで，ウェブなどでは，地図やグラフ等を 用いて，犯罪が集中する場所や時間帯の情報が提供されてきた． 「犯罪が集中する」ことの根拠として専ら用いられる指標は， 刑法犯認知件数である． この指標が特定の場所や時間帯に特に多 いことをもって，危険な場所や時間帯の存在が主張される． しかし，特定の場所や時間帯に犯罪が集中するということは， その場所や時間帯が 「犯罪に対する被害の可能性が高い」 という ことを必ずしも意味しない． 刑法犯認知件数の多さは， 単にその 場所や時間帯における潜在的な被害対象の数が多いことの反映 に過ぎない可能性があるためである． 例えば， 子供の性犯罪被害 は， 15～17 時の時間帯に多いとされる 1) が， この時間帯は子供の 外遊びの多い時間帯であり， 単に被害に遭いうる状況にある子供 の数が多いことの反映に過ぎないかもしれない． 同様に， 女性の 性犯罪被害は，2 時ころには少なくなる 1) が，この時間帯にはそ もそも外歩きをする女性が少ないことを考えると， むしろ被害に 遭う可能性は高いかもしれない．つまり， 「犯罪に対する被害の 可能性が高い」 ことを知るためには， 刑法犯認知件数だけでは不 十分であり， 犯罪被害に遭遇する可能性に対する曝露量を分母と した，被害リスク(確率)を求める必要がある 2) ． 犯罪の被害リスクは，住宅や事務所侵入盗等を想定した場合， 算出が容易である． ある地域における潜在的被害対象である住宅 や事務所の数は，既存統計や地図等から測ることができ，かつ， 地理的に固定されているためである． 潜在的被害対象の数がわか れば，それを被害の可能性に対する曝露量とみなして分母とし， 分子を刑法犯認知件数とすることで，被害リスクが求められる． しかし，粗暴犯等の対人犯罪になると，被害リスクの算出は 困難となる．潜在的被害対象である「人」が，時刻とともに移動 し，被害リスク算出の分母となる曝露量(曝露人口)を定めにく いためである(Denominator dilemma) 2) ．対人犯罪の被害リスク の算出においては， 慣例的には夜間人口が分母として用いられて きた(いわゆる「犯罪率」) ．しかし，夜間人口は，ある地域の居 住者の数であり， それをそのまま曝露人口とみなすことは， 特に 昼夜間で人口の違いが大きい地区でバイアスを生じさせる． ところで，時間とともに移動する人々の活動量を捉える試み は，交通分野では古くから行われてきた．とりわけ我が国では， パーソントリップ調査(PT 調査)に長い蓄積がある．PT 調査か らは， 人々の活動量を， 場所や時間と関連づけて推定することが できる．したがって，これを元に曝露人口を設定することで，対 人犯罪についても被害リスクを知ることができる可能性がある． 移動する人口(ambient population)を分母として被害リスクを 算出する試みには，1km メッシュ単位に整理された 24 時間平均 推計人口データ 3)-9) や，位置情報付きの Twitter データ・携帯電話 の測位データなど 10)-13) を分母として用い，被害リスクを求める ものがある．また，交通量を分母とし，路上強盗や粗暴犯の被害 リスクを算出する研究もある 14), 15) ．わが国でも，携帯電話の基 地局測位から推計された時間帯ごとの人口データを分母として 用い，街頭犯罪の被害リスクを求める研究 16) や，GPS による測 位とシミュレーションを組合せて場所ごとの時間人口を求め， そ れを分母として，子供の被害リスクを明らかにする研究 17) があ るが，研究例は極めて少ない． 本報告では，PT 調査データを用いて，犯罪被害の可能性に対 する曝露人口を考慮した性犯罪の被害リスクの算出を試みる．-297

title: Third-party policing approaches against organized crime: An evaluation of the yakuza exclusion ordinances
authors: Hoshino, Tetsuya, Kamada, Takuma
abstract: Third-party policing (TPP) refers to police efforts to persuade or coerce third parties to take some responsibility for crime control, prevention. The Yakuza Exclusion Ordinances (YEOs) of Japan aim to combat organized crime syndicates—the Yakuza. Consistent with the principles of TPP, the YEOs prohibit third parties (i.e., non-yakuza individuals) from providing any benefit to the yakuza. We argue that the effectiveness of the YEOs may depend on the strategic relationship among yakuza syndicates, where yakuza syndicates choose their power strategically to gain advantages over competition among rival yakuza syndicates.

title: Self-efficacy mechanism in human agency
authors: Bandura, Albert
abstract: Addresses the centrality of the self-efficacy mechanism (SEM) in human agency. SEM precepts influence thought patterns, actions,, emotional arousal. In causal tests, the higher the level of induced self-efficacy, the higher the performance accomplishments, the lower the emotional arousal. The different lines of research reviewed show that the SEM may have wide explanatory power. Perceived self-efficacy helps to account for such diverse phenomena as changes in coping behavior produced by different modes of influence, level of physiological stress reactions, self-regulation of refractory behavior, resignation, despondency to failure experiences, self-debilitating effects of proxy control, illusory inefficaciousness, achievement strivings, growth of intrinsic interest,, career pursuits. The influential role of perceived collective efficacy in social change, the social conditions conducive to development of collective inefficacy are analyzed. abstract: The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM; F. D. Davis, 1989), a derivative of the Theory of Reasoned Action (M. Fishbein, I. Ajzen, 1985), attempts to explain the psychological determinants of attitudes,, subsequent acceptance behavior, towards information technology in the workplace. The present study examined the efficacy of this psychologically based TAM within two samples of 108 government workers (aged 21–57 yrs) experienced in the use of computers. All Ss completed a self-report questionnaire consisting of both previously developed, purpose derived scales, measuring constructs such as computer anxiety, perceived usefulness, fun of using a computer, computer satisfaction, usage,, subjective norms. The study achieved its purpose of replicating, validating a development of the TAM, although only moderate support for the model was found. The applied implications of the research, wider theoretical implications of the study are discussed. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2013 APA, all rights reserved)
